comparison.relationship: Both files are closed loops of 176 points sampled on the same coordinate sequence with x2 = 7.50 * x1 (current_voltage coordinate ~7.5x larger). Switching is a smooth normalized polarization-like loop; current_voltage is a noisier raw electrical loop. Same-index correlation is near zero because the loop is traversed in the same direction, but on the monotonic ascending branch current_voltage is strongly proportional to the derivative of switching, consistent with current ~ rate of change of polarization.

findings: Both electrical files are closed loops; hysteresis is present in both.
Switching loop area (shoelace) = 9.2085; current_voltage loop area = 35703.63.
Coordinates are proportional: current_voltage coordinate = 7.50 * switching coordinate.
Same-index signal correlation = -0.001073; signals are independent traces at the same coordinates.
Switching is smooth/normalized (std 0.1567); current_voltage is noisy (std 78.3).
Derivative check: on the ascending branch current_voltage is strongly proportional to the derivative of switching (R2=0.9976, corr=0.9988).
Background (mean/min) subtraction leaves the shoelace hysteresis area essentially unchanged (shift-invariant).
Trimming 5% of the points changes the loop area by <3% for both files.
notes: loop_area computed via shoelace closed-polygon area (shift-invariant). Files share an identical 176-point coordinate sequence with a 7.5 scaling.
